newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-QUEENSLAND'S CANNON SUSPENDED FOR 15 WEEKS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-QUEENSLAND'S CANNON SUSPENDED FOR 15 WEEKS.

text.p: Queensland rugby union forward Brendan Cannon was suspended for 15 weeks on Sunday for stamping on a rival player in Saturday's bad-tempered Super 12 match against New South Wales, tournament officials said.

Reserve hooker Cannon was one of three players suspended by a hastily-convened Australian Rugby Union (ARU) judiciary panel, with New South Wales forward Richard Harry banned for three weeks and Queensland prop Dan Crowley for two.

The three-man ARU panel found Cannon guilty of dangerous play for stamping on New South Wales winger Alistair Murdoch in a second-half ruck. Murdoch continued playing with his head heavily bandaged after the incident.
Cannon's ban was the harshest given to a player since the tournament began last year. The Super 12 tournament features provincial sides from Australia, New Zealand and South Africa.
Harry was suspended for kneeing Queensland flyhalf Elton Flatley while Crowley was banned for punching New South Wales flanker and Wallaby team mate Michael Brial.
Brial will face the judiciary panel on Monday on an unspecified charge arising from the match.
Cannon was suspended until August 3, meaning he will miss Queensland's final three matches of the tournament.

New South Wales coach Matt Williams was quoted in newspapers on Sunday as saying that Crowley had entered the New South Wales dressing room after the match and tried to continue his fight with Brial before being pushed out of the room.
"(Crowley) came into the change room and said he wanted to carry it on," Williams said. "It was a totally disgraceful performance."
Last-placed Queensland scored only their second win from eight matches when they beat mid-table New South Wales 26-16.
